sources.title: The Witcher Season 4's Rotten Tomatoes Score Revealed - IMDb
highlights:
Season 4 arrived on Netflix earlier today, and the first wave of reviews has followed. They're decidedly mixed, with critics divided on Liam Hemsworth 's take on Geralt of Rivia (the actor replaces Henry Cavill in the role).Despite a positively reviewed second season, the series has never been a critical darling like Game of Thrones , for example. However, things are looking dire for The Witcher 's return, as its current Rotten Tomatoes score is a "Rotten" 56% based on 18 reviews. On the fan-generated "Popcornmeter," it has 18%.As a reminder, previous seasons have been scored 68% (Season 1), 95% (Season 2), and 79% (Season 3). A drop to 40% is steep, and suggests critics are ready to see the series end. See full article at ComicBookMovie.com

sources.title: The Witcher: Season 4 Debuts to a 20% Rotten Tomatoes Score
highlights:
October 2025

"This season feels like a parody of what The Witcher is supposed to be." As expected by most, given fans' reactions to its official trailer released a few weeks ago , the fourth season of Netflix's The Witcher TV adaptation has premiered to widespread disapproval and terrible review scores, with regular viewers and critics alike expressing their displeasure in Rotten Tomatoes scores. As of this writing, Season 4 sits at a dismal user score of just 20%, lower than Season 1's 46% and Season 2's 54% , and equal to Season 3, which also has 20% . When it comes to critic scores, the situation looks even more bleak for Netflix, as even critics – usually no strangers to giving high marks to mediocre works – lambasted the show's continuation, awarding it a 55% score, the lowest of any season of The Witcher. As for the "what went wrong?" part, reviews highlight two main reasons behind the overwhelmingly negative reception: Season 4's writing and poor character decisions, which contradicted the franchise's lore, clashed with The Witcher's tone, and made little sense from a storytelling standpoint, and miscasts – most notably the replacement of Geralt of Rivia's actor from Henry Cavill to Liam Hemsworth. ... portray the legendary character as effectively, an issue made even more glaring by the weak writing.
